title: China's Zhou Qunfei Tops Female Rich List with 127 Billion Yuan Fortune as Lens Technology Profit Halves
text:
China's Zhou Qunfei Tops Female Rich List with 127 Billion Yuan Fortune as Lens Technology Profit Halves — BigGo Finance Ask AI Real-time News Market Earnings Call Event Calendar Watchlist Podcast Influencer Tracker Earnings Call Event Calendar Watchlist Podcast Influencer Tracker More Ask AI Real-time News Watchlist Holdings Market Earnings Call Event Calendar Podcast Influencer Tracker China's Zhou Qunfei Tops Female Rich List with 127 Billion Yuan Fortune as Lens Technology Profit Halves
 Add preferred source The Hurun Research Institute released the 2026 Hurun Rich List on October 27, naming Lens Technology founder Zhou Qunfei as China's newest richest woman with a fortune of 127 billion yuan (approximately $19.0 billion). Combined with her husband Zheng Junlong, the couple's wealth totals 128 billion yuan (approximately $19.2 billion), ranking 33rd overall. Just two days before the list was unveiled, Lens Technology's third-quarter report showed revenue of 47.902 billion yuan (approximately $7.2 billion) for the first nine months, down 10.74% year-on-year, with net profit attributable to shareholders of 1.42 billion yuan (approximately $213.0 million), a 50.06% decline. Third-quarter net profit alone fell 50.42%. The company cited rising memory chip prices suppressing end demand, yuan appreciation hurting dollar-denominated revenue, and a shift in the autumn product launch schedule of a major customer. To counter the pressure, Lens Technology plans to acquire a 59.78% stake in PMG for $25 million; PMG's subsidiary is an Nvidia-certified server rack supplier. Key Elements 
 Zhou Qunfei Lens Technology Zheng Junlong Hurun Rich List Apple Nvidia PMG Zhejiang Yuanshi Liang Wenfeng DeepSeek Zhong Huijuan On October 27, the Hurun Research Institute released the 2026 Hurun Rich List, with Zhou Qunfei, founder of China's Lens Technology (300433.SZ), claiming the title of China's richest woman for the first time with a fortune of 127 billion yuan (approximately $19.0 billion). Together with her husband Zheng Junlong, the couple's combined wealth reaches 128 billion yuan (approximately $19.2 billion), placing them 33rd on the overall list. Yet just two days before the list was unveiled, the company known as a leader in the "Apple supply chain" reported that its net profit attributable to shareholders had fallen by more than half year-on-year.
 List data shows that Zhou Qunfei is this year's newly crowned richest woman. Last year, the position was held by Zhong Huijuan and her daughter Sun Yuan, founders of Hansoh Pharmaceutical, whose fortune then stood at 141 billion yuan (approximately $21.1 billion), with Zhou Qunfei ranking second at 110 billion yuan (approximately $16.5 billion). This year, the Zhong Huijuan family's wealth slipped to 124 billion yuan (approximately $18.6 billion), ranking 35th. Hurun reported that women entrepreneurs account for 23.2% of this year's list, up 0.8 percentage points from a year earlier, with more than 70% self-made — Zhou Qunfei among them.
 Public records show that Zhou Qunfei dropped out of middle school due to family poverty and went to work at Aoya Optical Glass Products Factory. In 1993, at age 23, she left the factory to start her own business, and in 2003 she formally founded Lens Technology. In 2006, the company began working with Apple, producing glass cover screens for the first-generation iPhone, and the following year it passed Apple's supplier certification, entering the "Apple supply chain." In 2015, Lens Technology listed on the ChiNext board of the Shenzhen Stock Exchange; in 2025 it also listed on the main board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, creating an "A+H" dual-capital-platform structure. The company's business now spans AI smart terminals, AI servers, commercial aerospace and optical interconnect, with 12 major R&D and production bases in Hunan, Guangdong, Jiangsu, Vietnam and Thailand. Its market value exceeds 140 billion yuan (approximately $21.0 billion).
 In stark contrast to the founder's rise to the top of the wealth rankings is the pressure on the company's operations. Lens Technology disclosed on the evening of October 25 that in the first nine months of this year it recorded operating revenue of 47.902 billion yuan (approximately $7.2 billion), down 10.74% year-on-year, and net profit attributable to shareholders of 1.42 billion yuan (approximately $213.0 million), down 50.06%. Third-quarter net profit attributable to shareholders was 843 million yuan (approximately $126.4 million), a year-on-year decline of 50.42%.
 Metric First Three Quarters of 2026 Year-on-Year Change 
 Operating revenue 47.902 billion yuan -10.74% 
 Net profit attributable to shareholders 1.42 billion yuan -50.06% 
 Q3 net profit attributable to shareholders 843 million yuan -50.42% 
 Note: Data from Lens Technology's third-quarter earnings announcement.
 Regarding the revenue decline, Lens Technology executives offered three explanations on an earnings call: during the reporting period, rising memory chip prices weighed on demand for smartphones and computer terminals, dragging down revenue from the company's related structural components, functional modules and assembly businesses; the continued appreciation of the yuan against the dollar hurt revenue from businesses settled mainly in dollars; and the autumn new-product launch schedule of a major customer was adjusted, shifting the recognition of related revenue accordingly.
 Industry sources in the consumer electronics supply chain said that, as a core supplier of exterior structural components to Apple, Lens Technology's reference to "a major customer's adjusted autumn new-product schedule" is widely understood in the industry to mean Apple. This autumn, Apple launched only the iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max and its first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo; the standard iPhone 18 was absent from the autumn launch event and is expected to hit the market only in spring 2027.
 Looking back at recent years, although Lens Technology's net profit has kept growing, the pace has slowed for several consecutive years. From 2022 to 2025, net profit attributable to shareholders was 2.448 billion yuan (approximately $367.2 million), 3.021 billion yuan (approximately $453.1 million), 3.624 billion yuan (approximately $543.6 million) and 4.018 billion yuan (approximately $602.7 million), with growth of 18.25%, 23.40%, 19.96% and 10.87%, respectively.
 Facing pressure on its core business, Lens Technology is accelerating its expansion into emerging strategic sectors. On October 16, the company announced plans to acquire a 59.78% stake in PMG for $25 million in cash (about 172 million yuan). PMG's controlled subsidiary, Zhejiang Yuanshi, is one of the server rack suppliers certified under Nvidia's RVL program. The move is seen by the market as an important step for the company into the AI computing hardware supply chain.
 Other changes on this year's rich list are also noteworthy. DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng entered the list for the first time, vaulting directly into the top ten with wealth of 280 billion yuan (approximately $42.0 billion). By region, the list includes 202 entrepreneurs from Zhejiang, 149 from Guangdong, 126 from Jiangsu, 77 from Hunan and 65 from Fujian, with Zhejiang natives forming the largest group. Entrepreneurs whose wealth fell the most include Xiaomi's Lei Jun (-157 billion yuan, ~-$23.5 billion), Nongfu Spring's Zhong Shanshan (-120 billion yuan, ~-$18.0 billion), Tencent's Pony Ma (-119 billion yuan, ~-$17.8 billion) and the Wang Ning family of Pop Mart (-94.5 billion yuan, ~-$14.2 billion). The list noted that these entrepreneurs' wealth has not truly shrunk to low levels but represents a rational pullback after rapid gains last year, and remains considerably higher than two years ago.
 Signs of broad pressure in the consumer sector are also reflected in the list: Pinduoduo's Colin Huang saw his wealth shrink by 112 billion yuan (approximately $16.8 billion), ranking 11th with 202 billion yuan (approximately $30.3 billion); Wahaha's Zong Fuli ranked 59th with 83.5 billion yuan (approximately $12.5 billion); Dongpeng Beverage's Lin Muqin and his son Lin Yupeng saw their wealth fall by 43 billion yuan (approximately $6.4 billion), making the list with 48 billion yuan (approximately $7.2 billion); and, hit by persistently low hog prices, Muyuan's Qin Yinglin and Qian Ying saw their wealth shrink by 32.5 billion yuan (approximately $4.9 billion), ranking 19th with 155 billion yuan (approximately $23.2 billion).
 For investors, Zhou Qunfei's rise to the top of the wealth rankings reflects more the capital market's pricing of Lens Technology's long-term value, while the halving of net profit in the third-quarter report reveals the reality of short-term fundamental pressure. Whether the company can open a second growth curve through new businesses such as AI server racks and restore profitability once its major customer's product schedule normalizes will be key for the market to watch going forward.
